summary.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin reported at about 4.3%, up from 3.5% in Q1; management sees 3.5% as steady-state margin.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 4.3%, up from 3.5% in Q1 and 3.6% in FY26, per the opening remarks (transcript is garbled and figures are partly unclear). The company opened a store in Jaipur, Rajasthan and a store in Nanded, Maharashtra, taking the network to 134 stores. Western India has grown to about 20% of revenue from about 5% a few years ago, with a potential of about 6 lakh MT in the next two years. Management framed steel price moves as broadly neutral in the quarter, after a roughly 10% inventory hit in Q1 when prices fell. Non-steel is targeted at 12-15% of revenue in about two years, with non-steel margin around 5% versus steel at 2.5-3%.

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.5% in Q1 FY27 and 3.6% in FY26
Added Jaipur (Rajasthan) and Nanded (Maharashtra) in the quarter
Up from ~5% a few years ago

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.5 to 3 crore per store (as stated)

segments.name: Steel tubes and pipes
segments.commentary: Core business; EBITDA margin about 2.5-3%. Management is pushing a better product mix within steel.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 5%. Target to raise share to about 12-15% of revenue in roughly two years.

segments.name: Western India
segments.commentary: Now about 20% of revenue, up from about 5% a few years ago; potential cited at 6 lakh MT in two years.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state EBITDA margin of about 3.5%, per management, with continued marketing spend needed for Rajasthan and other new states.
Non-steel to reach about 12-15% of total revenue in roughly two years.
Western region volume potential of about 6 lakh MT in the next two years, alongside volume targets of 1.2 and 1.45 (units not specified; likely million tonnes) in the coming years.
Store expansion described as strategic rather than blind; one store to be converted into a hybrid store in Kerala this year, with no other long-street expansion planned currently.
Store payback stated at around 4 to 5 years.
capex_capacity: New stores opened in Jaipur (Rajasthan) and Nanded (Maharashtra); total network 134 stores.
Store capex stated at around Rs 2.5 to 3 crore.
Store formats: steel, non-steel and hybrid; management says ROI is comparable across all three, with mix set by region.
Hybrid store conversion planned in Kerala for the current year.
demand_pricing: Management attributes margin resilience to network strength, a wider product range and aggressive growth in western India.
Competition has pushed the company to be more aggressive on marketing, which weighed on margins in the quarter.
Steel prices rose sharply in September, but other months were flat or lower; management says the net effect was neutral.
In Q1, falling steel prices caused an inventory hit of about 10% per an analyst's reference to management's comments.
Management says it is gaining share from smaller unorganised players and benefiting from infrastructure growth.
Gradual recovery in Karnataka market noted.

qa_highlights.question: Is 3.5% a fair steady-state EBITDA margin as volumes scale to 1.2 and 1.45 units?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed 3.5% is the steady-state target, citing continued marketing spend in Rajasthan and other new states, while noting aspirations to push higher.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin pressure in Q2 linked to marketing and steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and entry into new markets led to higher marketing spend; steel price moves were broadly neutral for the quarter after a sharp September rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-steel share outlook and the margin gap versus steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-steel targeted at 12-15% of revenue in about two years; non-steel margin about 5% versus steel at 2.5-3%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the store formats, payback and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Formats are steel, non-steel and hybrid, with ROI comparable across formats; payback about 4-5 years; capex about Rs 2.5-3 crore per store.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Rajasthan rather than deepen Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entry was driven by a strong regional manager willing to take on the state, under its team-based model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose the retail and non-retail split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the split, saying it now reports by vertical; it declined to share more customer-level data.

risks_watch: Marketing intensity rising in new states (Rajasthan, Western India) could keep margins below the 4%+ level seen in Q2.
Steel price volatility: a falling market produced about a 10% inventory hit in Q1 per the call.
Transcript quality is poor; the reported 4.3% margin, the volume figures (1.2, 1.45, 6 lakh MT) and the Q1 inventory-hit figure should be verified against the filing before use.
Non-steel ramp to 12-15% of revenue is a multi-year aspiration with no quantified plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and western expansion, but guarded on margins: management called 3.5% a steady-state level and tied it to ongoing marketing spend. Answers on store-level data and retail/non-retail split were evasive.
key_quotes: 3.5% is our steady state is what we are looking to.
